subject.title: RFC: Distributed Agent Runtime — separate control plane from agent compute

question: Should OpenClaw pursue a core Gateway/control-plane and per-agent runtime split, and if so which first milestone should be supported?
rationale: The remaining work requires choosing public protocol, config, security, lifecycle, session-state, delivery, and migration boundaries; automation cannot safely pick those product and security contracts.

options.title: Approve phased runtime split
options.body: Keep this issue as the canonical RFC and sponsor a first milestone that defines protocol, trust model, and local-split lifecycle before container or Kubernetes runners.

options.title: Narrow to execution placement
options.body: Treat the worker-runtime experiment and execution-backend placement work as the current scope while deferring the broader Gateway split.

options.title: Defer core architecture change
options.body: Continue improving single-Gateway, multi-Gateway, worker, and plugin or harness slices without committing to a distributed runtime boundary yet.

recommendation.title: Approve phased runtime split
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the canonical RFC and sponsor a first milestone that defines protocol, trust model, and local-split lifecycle before container or Kubernetes runners.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest overlap across current agent runtime refactors, the source-grounded runtime docs, and the active worker-runtime experiment.
